meta.title: Rebasely — Git and Perforce, in one workspace
meta.description: Rebasely is an open-source desktop client for Git and Perforce. Review text and image diffs, stage precise commits, manage changelists, and explore history on macOS and Windows.

features.label: Made for your workflow

features.review.body: Read unified or split diffs, compare images, and stage a file, a hunk, or individual lines in Git.

principles.title: Your tools. Your workflow.
principles.cli.title: Built on your command-line tools
principles.cli.body: Rebasely runs Git and the Perforce CLI. Your repository configuration, hooks, and existing tool behavior remain part of the workflow.
principles.local.title: Diagnostics stay local
principles.local.body: Diagnostic files are stored on your device and are not uploaded automatically. You choose what to share when reporting a problem.
principles.open.title: Open to inspection
principles.open.body: Read the source, build the app, or contribute a focused improvement. Rebasely is open source under the MIT License.
start.title: Bring your next project.
start.step1.title: Install your tools.
start.step1.body: Download Rebasely. Install Git for Git repositories, or the Perforce CLI for Perforce workspaces.
start.step2.title: Open your workspace.
start.step2.body: Open, clone, or create a Git repository. Connect an existing Perforce client, or create a workspace from a stream or depot path.
start.step3.title: Make the next change.
start.step3.body: Choose a file, review the difference, and prepare your commit or changelist.
faq.title: A few useful details.
faq.systems.question: Which platforms can I download?
faq.systems.answer: The release provides macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64 builds. The source can also be built on Linux with the Tauri platform prerequisites.
faq.tools.question: Do I need Git or Perforce installed?
faq.tools.answer: Yes. Install Git for Git repositories, and the Perforce command-line client (p4) for Perforce workspaces. You can select their executables in Settings.
faq.accounts.question: Where are my repositories stored?
faq.accounts.answer: Your local repositories and workspace files stay on your device. Remote Git and Perforce operations connect to the servers you configure using the underlying command-line tools.
faq.demo.question: Is this an actual repository in the demo?
faq.demo.answer: The website demo is a browser-local example with invented data. Staging, committing, shelving, and submitting in the demo never change a real repository.
